questions.prompt: Which statement about a point cloud is correct?
options: The order of the points carries the neighbourhood information, as in an image.
It is always a dense grid of depth values.
Every cloud has the same density regardless of sensor distance.
The points are an unordered set, so neighbours must be computed from geometry.
questions.explanation: A point cloud is an unordered set; shuffling rows changes nothing, so neighbours come from a k-d tree or voxel grid.

questions.prompt: Points (0.12,0.31),(0.18,0.39),(0.55,0.02),(0.58,0.07) are voxel-downsampled with voxel size 0.2. How many voxels are occupied?
Source centroid is (1,0), target centroid (2,1), rotation is 30 degrees. Give the x component of t = c_Q - R c_P to 3 decimals.
Why does a least-squares rigid fit with known pairs get dragged by one gross outlier?
options: Squared residuals give a large residual a large weight, so the minimiser moves toward it.
Kabsch averages the residuals instead of squaring them, so every point has equal weight.
Centroids ignore the outlier automatically, but the rotation is then chosen at random.
Kabsch discards pairs with residual above 1, so an outlier changes which points are kept.
questions.explanation: Squared error grows quadratically with residual, so the fit compromises toward the outlier. Centroids are means, which are not robust either.

questions.prompt: ICP converged with a small final RMSE but the pose is 20 degrees off. Most likely cause?
options: It converged to a local minimum from a poor initial guess or degenerate geometry.
The cost can only decrease, so a small RMSE implies correct pose.
Nearest-neighbour search is exact, so ICP is globally optimal.
questions.explanation: ICP is a local method; a good-looking residual does not prove global correctness.

questions.prompt: Ten pairs agree under translation (1,0) except one target displaced a further 5 in x. The estimate is the mean offset. What x translation is estimated?
You must register a lidar scan of a long straight corridor to the previous one. Describe what could go wrong and how you would detect and mitigate it.
rubric: Names the degeneracy: no constraint along the corridor axis, so ICP slides.
Gives a detection method, for example the eigenvalues of the constraint matrix or comparison against odometry.
Gives a mitigation: other sensors or priors, structure with axial features, or rejecting the update.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
